summary: Preemptive GPU rebalance triggers transparent variant swap and tokenizer mismatch for pinned sessions
description: Issue summary: During an autoscaler-initiated GPU rebalancing event in the customer's dedicated pool, a subset of pinned sessions were transparently routed to a quantized fallback variant. The fallback model uses a different tokenizer configuration which produced tokenization deltas for multi-turn chat prompts and caused degraded completion coherence. Impact: Several paying tenants at Clairvoyant Health observed mixed model outputs, elevated token counts (billing spike), and streaming disconnects for long-lived pinned sessions. Customer-visible window: ~2026-03-10T02:12:00Z - 2026-03-10T02:48:00Z.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer has dedicated pool with pinned model redwood-3b-v1 and active sticky sessions.
2) Simulate autoscaler preemption of a set of GPUs (force-orchestrator-rebalance) while traffic remains steady.
3) Observe routing decision: some session tokens are reassigned to nodes running redwood-3b-quantized-v1 due to transient capacity constraints.
4) Replay identical multi-turn prompt to pinned session and compare tokenization/response differences between variants.
5) Verify that edge proxy did not surface explicit pin-lift events; routing change is transparent to client.
Note: reproduces reliably in staging when autoscaler preemption frequency > 1/min and prewarm disabled.
logs: [2026-03-10T02:12:12Z] serving-runtime[warn]: session_reassign session_id=abc123 old_node=gpu-12 new_node=gpu-34 reason=capacity_threshold downstream_variant=redwood-3b-quantized-v1
[2026-03-10T02:30:01Z] billing[metric]: token_count spike customer=ClairvoyantHealth delta_tokens=+47% window=00:20:00
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: orchestration preemption caused pinned session to be moved without explicit unpin handshake.
Edge observation: edge-proxy still returned pin header; however request routing ended up at a node where only quantized variant was available (prewarm pool had been partially evaporated).

We observed tokenizer config mismatch between redwood-3b-v1 and redwood-3b-quantized-v1: vocabulary normalization differences produced off-by-one tokenization and extra EOS tokens for some multi-turn prompts.

Orchestrator logs show fast path reassign (ttl-based) that bypasses pin-coherence gate when node capacity < 2 active replicas; this was hit because autoscaler preempted 4/8 GPUs in the customer's pool in a short window.

Correlation with billing: token_count telemetry aligns with period where requests were served by quantized variant; tokenization delta explains part of the increase but not the full 47% (further analysis ongoing for short-circuiting retries).
Repro steps executed in staging reproduced the transparent swap when prewarm disabled; enabling prewarm prevented swap in the same scenario.

Temporary mitigation: orchestration change to prefer maintaining at least one replica with original variant during preemption waves for pinned cohorts; applied as emergency config for Clairvoyant Health and monitored.

Next actions: (a) patch orchestrator to respect explicit pin handshake as higher-priority constraint than aggressive preemption; (b) add detection/alert when tokenization profile changes between served variants; (c) create a rollback plan for customers impacted by billing spike.
Assigned owners: Marcus Lee (SRE/Orchestrator), Priya Nair (Serving Runtime), Zoe Kim (Customer Success)
Estimated ETA for orchestrator hotfix: 2026-03-13 (code + canary).

resolution: Mitigation applied: emergency orchestrator config reduced preemption aggressiveness for the customer's dedicated pool and prevented further transparent swaps. Hotfix merged to ensure pin-handshake is honored above preemption when pool capacity is ephemeral; canary deployed and under observation. Root cause: orchestrator preemption logic performed fast-path reassignments that did not consult pin-coherence constraints when available_replicas < threshold, combined with variant tokenizer divergence. Follow-ups: permanent orchestrator patch, tokenizer alignment for quantized builds, retroactive billing credits for token delta. Owner for postmortem and billing reconciliation: Zoe Kim.
